Messages.Author: Bloodartist
Messages.Body:
Haqim's law: retribution is another new, strong, clan-specific card. I applaud this sort of card design. It basically looks to create a new deck archetype, which I really like. This is what VTES needs to keep the game moving forward.

Its very useful that BH now have a way to cycle their combat cards without getting into combat. Also cycle a combat card during bleed hoping to hit another bleed card..

Hunter's mark is a card that may find its way into other decks than BH... Made me go check what did Thaumaturgy have in the "can't be used during first round" department..

Hunger of marduk is practically better than taste of vitae for rush decks that can play it, since it can't be avoided, unlike taste (which can be avoided by preventing the damage).

However, Banu are still lacking in damage prevention, which is probably the biggest reason why they won't become "too" strong. But regardless gotta give big thumbs up for the designers and playtesters.

ps. You are missing some line breaks there..

Messages.Author: Hobbesgoblin
Messages.Body:
Hunger of marduk has to be played before range, telegraphing your intentions.

This is more relevant in the Guns+taste Case, as, when you plan on gunning and tasting, if you get hit by a S:CE, you simply don't taste, while the hunger of marduk already has to be played at that time.

In comparison to taste, the difference is primarily, that in the case of not being the acitng minion, taste is better, as you announce your strike last.

For starters, let me say that I originally misread hunger of marduk... I thought it was just theft of 2 in prerange (kind of like outside the hourglass). That would've been cool. I still consider it to be the better card than theft, although that's because I place much lesser value to hiding information than most people here. For me, cards are not "wasted", but rather "cycled". My decks tend to be proactive and feature good cardflow.

As for the justicar, I agree that this ability is weak. In general putting politically-aligned abilities on a combat vampire is weird. Its never been a thing... (I remember like one other vampire that had similar ability and it has never done much anything).

Im also not a huge fan of two random parity shifts in the deck. Chances of these going through are negligible, because these days random titles for vote defense is very common. We just had a discussion about this on the Finnish discord.

I believe this justicar would function best in a stealth voter deck with other clans, where his ability would be supplementary. NOT this Banu Haqim deck.

Messages.Author: Bloodartist
Messages.Body:
> Lemminkäinen wrote:
> So I'm slowly crawling out of torpor and am trying to make sense of everything - a stupid question that probably has an answer in some very obvious place but I wasn't able to find it: Can Banu Haqim use Assamite clan cards and vice versa?
>
Banu Haqim and Assamites are considered the same clan for purposes of cards.
Followers of Set and the Ministry are considered the same clan for purposes of cards.

You can use their clan cards interchangeably.

The biggest thing to note about the V5 vampires is their new clan discipline spreads:
Banu Haqim: thaumaturgy, obfuscate, celerity
Ministry: protean, presence, obfuscate
Ravnos: Animalism, obfuscate, presence
Salubri: Auspex, dominate, fortitude
Tzimisce: Animalism, dominate, protean.
Lasombra: Dominate, Oblivion, potence.

Basically the RPG is doing away with clan-specific disciplines. Now those disciplines are becoming a combo of two other disciplines, with the exception of Oblivion which replaces obtenebration I think. (Hecate will have oblivion also afaik) I believe in VTES obtenebration and oblivion are the same discipline, but don't quote me on that.

Another thing to note is how dominate got a whole lot more common...

The official card list has updated text on appropriate cards I believe.
